memory_update.text: ORCL should be treated as a demand validator and capacity builder, not a direct supply-chain chokepoint; monitor RPO conversion, lease commitments, capex and power-secured data-center capacity.

EQIX and DLR are data-center capacity/interconnection mappings where scarcity depends on power-ready sites, liquid-cooling capability and interconnection availability rather than generic square footage.

STX and WDC have stronger-than-initial Layer 1 evidence as secondary AI infrastructure chokepoints because nearline HDD capacity appears tight and AI/cloud workloads increase exabyte-scale storage needs.

CAT and CMI have direct evidence of data-center-driven power-generation demand; they should be grouped with backup/bridge power and large-engine/generator bottlenecks rather than generic industrial machinery.
GNRC has plausible C&I generator and packaging exposure to data centers, but needs direct order, backlog and customer evidence before being ranked with CAT/CMI.

ENPH relevance improved after announcing an AI-data-center solid-state-transformer platform, but evidence remains early-stage product-option evidence without orders, certification or customer validation.

FSLR maps to hyperscaler clean-power procurement and domestic solar supply, but intermittency means it is not a firm-power chokepoint unless tied to storage, grid interconnection or contracted data-center PPAs.
SBAC should remain deprioritized for this theme unless filings reveal measurable edge-compute, AI workload, private wireless or data-center-adjacent revenue.

Need entity-status verification for NEP/XPLR and asset-level proof that any renewable PPAs or infrastructure assets are directly tied to AI data-center loads; parent NEE evidence should not be automatically assigned to NEP.
Market-pricing checks remain missing for this chunk: relative performance, valuation expansion, earnings revisions, short interest and whether AI-power/storage narratives are already crowded.

summary: Layer 2B maps the candidate chunk into ticker-to-node relationships for the 'New Hotspots' theme, with emphasis on AI infrastructure demand validation, data-center power availability, nearline storage constraints, backup/primary generation, and second-order clean/distributed energy exposure. The strongest relationships in this chunk are ORCL as a demand-side AI cloud capacity buyer/builder, EQIX and DLR as power-constrained data-center capacity operators, STX and WDC as nearline HDD supply-chain beneficiaries, and CAT/CMI/GNRC as data-center power-generation equipment suppliers. SBAC, NEP and, to a lesser extent, FSLR remain indirect. ENPH was upgraded from peripheral speculation to a low-evidence product-option relationship because it announced an AI-data-center solid-state-transformer platform, but commercial validation remains missing.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check Oracle's latest 10-Q/10-K footnotes for lease commitments, cloud capacity obligations, capex, concentration of AI customers, and any disclosure on power-secured data-center capacity.
ticker_relationships.node: AI compute demand and cloud capacity
ticker_relationships.relationship: Oracle is a demand-side AI infrastructure participant: rapid OCI/IaaS growth and very large RPO indicate customer commitments for cloud and AI capacity, which can validate upstream demand for data centers, GPUs, networking, power, cooling and leases. It is not a pure bottleneck supplier; the key relationship is that Oracle converts AI demand into physical capacity commitments and power/data-center procurement needs.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Pull Q1/Q2 2026 company filings and presentation details for xScale pre-leasing, MW capacity, power availability by market, liquid-cooling retrofits, capex per MW and churn/renewal spreads.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Equinix maps to the data-center capacity/interconnection node. AI demand increases the value of power-ready, connectivity-rich sites and xScale/IBX capacity, while power density, liquid cooling and regional utility constraints affect deployment timing and returns.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify lease terms, delivery dates, MW under construction, power-secured inventory, customer concentration and markets where utility interconnection delays could defer revenue.
ticker_relationships.node: Hyperscale leasing, data-center real estate and power-constrained markets
ticker_relationships.relationship: Digital Realty maps to hyperscale data-center leasing and interconnection capacity. Its record AI-oriented leasing and backlog make it a demand validator, but the bottleneck exposure depends on whether it controls scarce powered land/capacity rather than merely adding commoditized shell capacity.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Search company filings and transcripts for edge-compute, small-cell, private wireless, data-center interconnect or AI workload references; otherwise keep deprioritized.
ticker_relationships.node: Wireless towers and optional edge-compute adjacency
ticker_relationships.relationship: SBA Communications is a peripheral digital-infrastructure candidate. Its core tower-leasing model is tied primarily to wireless carrier capex, spectrum and mobile-network densification, not directly to AI data-center power chokepoints. Edge-AI relevance remains unproven.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Validate nearline capacity allocation, customer LTAs, HAMR/Mozaic ramp, exabyte shipments, average price per TB, inventory, and whether AI/cloud demand is replacing or adding to normal cloud storage demand.
ticker_relationships.node: Nearline HDD and exabyte-scale data-center storage
ticker_relationships.relationship: Seagate maps to AI-adjacent mass storage. AI training, inference logs, data lakes, checkpoints and archival datasets can increase exabyte-scale nearline HDD demand; capacity allocation and pricing discipline can make HDD a secondary supply-chain chokepoint.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Confirm post-separation segment exposure, customer purchase orders, 2026/2027 LTAs, enterprise share of revenue, pricing, supply constraints and capacity-expansion limits.
ticker_relationships.node: Nearline HDD, enterprise data storage and AI data lakes
ticker_relationships.relationship: Western Digital maps to the same nearline HDD/data-center storage bottleneck as Seagate. Evidence suggests strong enterprise/cloud storage demand and constrained 2026 HDD capacity, but the thesis should separate HDD from flash/NAND exposure and account for the completed HDD/flash separation.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track Power & Energy backlog, large-engine capacity expansion, data-center order mix, margin sustainability, generator lead times, emissions/permitting constraints and competition from Cummins, mtu/Rolls-Royce, Kohler and gas-turbine suppliers.
ticker_relationships.node: Data-center backup and primary power generation equipment
ticker_relationships.relationship: Caterpillar maps to large reciprocating engines, turbines and construction equipment used in data-center buildout and alternative power solutions. Compared with generic construction exposure, the clearer node is Power & Energy demand from data centers and cloud/AI power needs.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify Power Systems backlog, generator capacity, regional demand by U.S./China, data-center customer mix, order-to-revenue timing, emissions rules and pricing versus component cost inflation.
ticker_relationships.node: Backup generators, power systems and data-center power equipment
ticker_relationships.relationship: Cummins maps to the data-center backup/prime power generation node. Power Systems growth and guidance tied to data-center demand suggest direct exposure, but the degree of bottleneck control depends on generator set capacity, engines, alternators, packaging partners and customer qualification.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check direct data-center revenue disclosures, Enercon backlog, MW-scale generator packaging capacity, hyperscaler/colocation customer wins, margin impact and whether demand is standby backup or primary/bridge power.
ticker_relationships.node: Commercial and industrial backup power, generator packaging and distributed generation
ticker_relationships.relationship: Generac maps to commercial/industrial generators and packaged power systems. Its relevance improved if data-center demand drives C&I generator sales and if the Enercon acquisition expands large-MW packaging capability, but product fit must be checked against hyperscale scale requirements.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Look for SST technical specs, voltage/current ratings, qualification partners, pilot customers, revenue timing, UL/IEEE certification, thermal performance, and competition from Eaton, Schneider, Siemens, ABB and medium-voltage specialists.
ticker_relationships.node: Distributed energy, grid-edge power electronics and AI-data-center solid-state transformer option
ticker_relationships.relationship: Enphase remains mostly peripheral to the AI power chokepoint, but Q1 2026 disclosure of an IQ SST platform purpose-built for AI data centers creates a new optional relationship to data-center power electronics. Evidence is product-announcement level, not order/backlog level.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Identify whether backlog counterparties include hyperscaler-linked projects, co-located data-center power projects, utility PPAs in data-center-heavy regions, and whether storage/firming partners convert solar into usable firm capacity.
ticker_relationships.node: Domestic utility-scale solar modules and hyperscaler clean-power procurement
ticker_relationships.relationship: First Solar maps to clean-power supply for utility-scale generation that may support hyperscaler PPAs and grid decarbonization. The relationship is indirect because solar does not solve firm 24/7 power by itself, but domestic module capacity and contracted backlog can matter where hyperscalers procure renewable energy at scale.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify current entity name/ticker status, asset mix, PPA counterparties, sponsor dropdown pipeline, refinancing needs, distribution policy and whether any contracts are directly tied to data-center load.
ticker_relationships.node: Renewable infrastructure PPAs and financing vehicle exposure
ticker_relationships.relationship: NextEra Energy Partners, now operating under XPLR Infrastructure branding in some materials, maps only indirectly to AI data-center demand through renewable PPAs and contracted clean-energy assets. Financing structure, sponsor relationship and distribution/deleveraging issues may dominate the AI-power narrative.
